_what: Nominal filament shrinkage, per material, as an Orca/SuperSlicer scale percentage.
_units: filament_shrink is a SCALE FACTOR: 100% means no compensation, 100.3% scales the model up by 0.3% so the cooled part lands on nominal. PrusaSlicer expresses the SAME thing as the shrinkage percentage itself -- its own tooltip reads 'if you measured 99mm instead of 100mm, enter 1%' -- so PrusaSlicer's value is ours minus 100. The emitter does that transform; do not pre-subtract here.
_why_not_100: Every vendor in the entire OrcaSlicer profile tree ships filament_shrink at 100% -- 64 files checked, not one populated. That is a default nobody filled in, not a finding that plastics do not shrink. Shipping 100% means every part comes out systematically undersized by the material's shrinkage.
_status: NOMINAL, NOT MEASURED. These are polymer-class typicals, chosen mid-range from the published spread for each family. Real shrinkage on this machine is also a function of chamber temperature, bed temperature and cooling, and the Zero runs a hot small enclosure -- so treat these as a starting point that is right in sign and order of magnitude, and replace them per material with measured values. Procedure: notes/runbook-flow-and-shrinkage.md.
_z_axis: Deliberately left at 0 for every material. Z error on an FDM part is dominated by first-layer squish and layer-height quantisation, not by polymer shrinkage, and scaling Z breaks the relationship between commanded and actual layer height. Both slicers default it to no compensation and we keep that. Settable per material here if a measurement ever justifies it.

PLA Silk.note: PLA base polymer, treated as PLA

ABS.note: strongly chamber-dependent; the Zero's hot enclosure should put it at the low end

TPU.note: least reliable of the set -- elastomers recover dimensionally over hours and a single caliper reading is not the whole story
